title: Property tax schedule for 2026-27, effective 1 April 2026
text: This schedule applies to all assessed properties in the North, South, East and Central zones of the city from 1 April 2026 and replaces the 2024-26 property tax schedule. Property tax is levied on carpet area at an annual base rate per square foot that depends on the location category of the street: ₹3.20 on Category A streets, ₹2.60 on Category B streets and ₹2.10 on Category C streets. The base amount is multiplied by a usage factor of 1.0 for residential, 2.5 for commercial and 1.5 for institutional use, and by an age factor of 0.8 for buildings more than 25 years old. Tax is payable in two half-yearly instalments: the first half-year instalment is due by 31 July and the second half-year instalment is due by 31 January. The early payment rebate has been withdrawn from 2026-27, so no rebate is given for paying the full year in advance, even before the first due date. Vacancy remission is not available: a residential or commercial building that is locked, empty or unlet is taxed in full, because the remission for vacant buildings was discontinued with this schedule. Owner-occupied homes of senior citizens aged 60 or above get a 10 percent concession on the residential tax for up to 1,000 square feet of carpet area. A penalty of 2 percent per month or part of a month is charged on any instalment that is unpaid after its due date. A solid waste user charge of ₹60 per month for each residential unit is collected along with property tax and shown as a separate line on the bill.

title: Property tax schedule for 2024-26 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 April 2026 by the 2026-27 property tax schedule. This page is kept only because arrears for 2024-25 and 2025-26 are still worked out on it. Base rates per square foot of carpet area were ₹2.90 on Category A streets, ₹2.35 on Category B streets and ₹1.90 on Category C streets, with the same usage factors as today. The two half-yearly instalments were due by 30 June and 31 December. A rebate of 10 percent of the year's general tax was given when the full year was paid by 30 April. Under this schedule a residential building that stayed vacant for more than 90 consecutive days could get a vacancy remission of 50 percent of the general tax, if the owner applied at the ward office within 30 days of the end of the half-year. The penalty on late instalments was 1.5 percent per month. The senior citizen concession was 10 percent for up to 750 square feet of carpet area. Penalty on arrears from these years continues to be charged at the rate in force for the year the arrears belong to, not at the current rate.

title: Self-assessment returns, survey checks and objections
text: An owner must file a self-assessment return for a new building within 60 days of completion or occupation, whichever is earlier, and must file a fresh return whenever the carpet area or the use of the building changes by more than 10 percent. Returns can be filed on the citizen portal or at the ward office, and the declared carpet area must exclude external walls, common staircases and open terraces. Survey teams check declared areas using drone maps and site visits. If the surveyed carpet area exceeds the declared area by more than 5 percent, the owner pays the difference in tax for up to the previous 3 years, plus a penalty equal to twice the difference for the current year. If a residential building is found in commercial use without a fresh return, the commercial rate applies from the date of the survey and a flat penalty of ₹5,000 is added. Objections to a revised assessment can be filed with the zonal assessment officer within 30 days of the notice, with a fee of ₹100, but the undisputed portion of the tax must be paid first. A second appeal lies to the tax appeals bench within 60 days of the zonal order. Name transfer of a property in the tax record after a sale costs 0.1 percent of the registered sale value, with a minimum of ₹500 and a maximum of ₹10,000, if applied for within 3 months of registration.

title: Registration of births and deaths, and certificate copies
text: A birth or death that happens within city limits is registered at the ward office of the ward where it happened, not the ward where the family lives. Hospitals and nursing homes report births and deaths on their premises directly, and the family only collects the certificate. Home births and deaths must be reported by the head of the household. Registration within 21 days is free, and the first copy of the certificate is issued free. Registration between 22 and 30 days carries a late fee of ₹25. From 31 days up to one year, registration needs a late fee of ₹75, an affidavit on plain paper, and the written permission of the zonal registrar, which is given only at the zone office on Tuesdays and Fridays. After one year an order from a first class magistrate is required and the late fee is ₹150. Additional copies of a birth or death certificate cost ₹50 per copy and are ready within 3 working days. Digitally signed certificates with a QR code can also be downloaded from the portal at ₹20 per download and are valid in the same way as printed ones. A child's name can be added free of charge within 12 months of registration, and for ₹50 after that, up to 15 years from the date of birth.

title: Trade licences: three-year licence, effective 1 April 2025
text: From 1 April 2025, trade licences are issued for a block of three financial years, and there is no annual renewal. This replaces the one-year trade licence that had to be renewed every March. The fee for the whole three-year block is paid when the licence is issued: ₹1,800 for shops and offices up to 200 square feet, ₹4,500 for 201 to 500 square feet, and ₹9,000 above 500 square feet. Eating places pay double these amounts, and trades that store LPG, chemicals or fireworks also need a fire safety certificate before a licence is issued. A licence taken out part way through a block runs to the end of that block, and the fee is reduced by one third for each full financial year already over. New licences are issued within 15 working days of a complete application. Renewal for the next block must be applied for at least 30 days before the licence expires. Trading on an expired licence attracts a penalty of 25 percent of the fee for each quarter or part of a quarter. Changing the trade name or adding a partner costs ₹500. The licence certificate must be displayed at the premises. A GST registration or a shop and establishment registration does not replace the trade licence.

title: Building plan approval routes and timelines
text: Residential buildings on plots of up to 300 square metres, with no more than ground plus two floors and a height of up to 10 metres, can be approved through the self-certification route. A registered architect uploads the plans and certifies that they comply with the building bye-laws, and the approval is issued within 7 working days of the online submission. All other buildings, and any residential plot above 300 square metres, follow the regular route: a site inspection is done and the approval is issued within 30 working days of a complete application. There is no deemed approval on either route; if the time limit is missed, the application is escalated to the city engineer. The scrutiny fee is ₹15 per square metre of total built-up area, payable on submission. An approval is valid for 3 years and can be extended once for 2 more years for a fee of ₹2,000. The owner must ask for a plinth inspection within 7 days of completing the plinth, and construction above the plinth cannot continue until it is cleared. Self-certified approvals are audited at random, and if the plans are found non-compliant the architect's registration can be suspended and the building can be sealed. Occupancy certificates are issued within 15 working days of the completion certificate.

title: Domestic water and sewer connections and tariff
text: This page covers houses and residential buildings. A new 15 mm, or half inch, domestic water connection costs ₹4,200, including the meter. A 20 mm connection, required for buildings with more than four flats, costs ₹7,500. A domestic sewer connection costs ₹2,800 per property. Where the connection needs a public road to be cut, a road restoration charge is billed separately at ₹1,100 per running metre for tar roads and ₹1,600 per running metre for concrete roads. Connections are released only in the name of the owner shown in the property tax record; a tenant can be added as a billing contact. New connections are released within 15 working days of payment. Domestic water is metered and billed monthly at ₹6 per kilolitre for the first 15 kilolitres, ₹11 per kilolitre from 15 to 30 kilolitres, and ₹20 per kilolitre above 30 kilolitres, with a minimum charge of ₹90 per month. Supply times are 6 am to 8 am in the North and East zones and 5:30 am to 7:30 am in the South and Central zones, and supply moves to alternate days from April to June. A household may not fit a booster pump directly on the service line; the fine is ₹2,000 and the pump is seized.

title: Commercial and institutional water and sewer connections
text: This page covers shops, hotels, hospitals, schools, offices and other non-domestic premises. A new 15 mm commercial water connection costs ₹9,000, including the meter, and a 20 mm connection costs ₹14,000. Connections above 20 mm need a hydraulic assessment by the water works engineer and are priced separately. A commercial sewer connection costs ₹6,500 per property, and premises that discharge kitchen or workshop waste must fit a grease trap before the sewer connection is released. Road restoration charges are the same as for domestic connections. Commercial water is billed monthly at a flat ₹40 per kilolitre, with a minimum charge of ₹600 per month, and there is no slab system. Commercial connections are released within 21 working days of payment. A security deposit equal to three months' minimum charge is collected with the connection charge and refunded when the connection is closed. Hotels and hospitals using more than 50 kilolitres a day must have a separate underground storage sump, and supply to them can be reduced during summer shortages before domestic supply is reduced.

title: Household solid waste collection schedule and rules
text: Door-to-door collection vehicles cover every ward between 7 am and 11 am. Wet waste, meaning kitchen and food waste, is collected every day, including Sundays. Dry waste is collected only on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and it is not picked up on other days, so households should store paper, plastic, metal, glass and cloth until then. Sanitary waste such as diapers and sanitary pads must be wrapped in newspaper, marked with a red cross, and handed over in a separate bag with the wet waste on any day. Domestic hazardous waste, such as batteries, tube lights, expired medicines and paint cans, is collected on the first Saturday of each month. Waste that is not segregated is refused after one warning, and households are fined ₹200 for a first offence and ₹500 for each repeat. Burning waste in the open carries a fine of ₹5,000, and littering in public places carries a fine of ₹500. If the collection vehicle misses a street, a complaint made before noon gets the waste collected the same day by 5 pm. The solid waste user charge of ₹60 per month per residential unit is collected with property tax.

title: Bulk waste, garden waste and construction debris pickup
text: Households can book a bulk waste pickup for old furniture, mattresses, large appliances and garden cuttings through the helpline or the portal, at least 48 hours in advance. Each residential property gets two free bulk pickups per financial year, each of up to one cubic metre, and any further pickup costs ₹400. Construction and demolition debris is not covered by the free pickups: it is charged at ₹1,200 per tractor load of about 2.5 cubic metres and is collected within 3 working days of booking. Dumping debris on a road, drain or vacant plot carries a fine of ₹10,000 and the cost of removal. Electronic waste is taken only at the e-waste collection drive held on the second Sunday of every month at the four zone offices. Housing societies with more than 100 flats, and premises producing more than 100 kg of waste a day, are bulk generators and must compost or process their wet waste on site; they get a 5 percent rebate on the solid waste user charge once on-site processing is certified by the ward sanitary inspector.

title: Pet dog and cat registration
text: Every pet dog and every pet cat kept within city limits must be registered with the veterinary section, and the registration must be renewed every year by 30 April. Registration costs ₹500 per year for each dog and ₹150 per year for each cat. The fee is waived for indie dogs and cats adopted from a registered shelter or animal welfare group, and for sterilised strays taken in as pets. Registration must be done within 30 days of getting the pet, or within 30 days of the animal turning three months old. The owner needs a valid anti-rabies vaccination certificate, a recent photo of the animal and proof of address. A metal tag with the registration number is issued, and it must be worn on the collar in public places. Keeping an unregistered dog carries a fine of ₹1,000, and keeping an unregistered cat carries a fine of ₹300. Owners must clean up after their pets in parks and on streets, or pay a fine of ₹500. Commercial breeders and pet shops need a separate trade licence and are not covered by pet registration.

title: Marriage registration
text: Marriages solemnised within city limits, or where either spouse lives within city limits, can be registered at any zone office. Both spouses and two witnesses must appear in person with original documents: proof of age for both spouses, such as a birth certificate, a school leaving certificate or a passport; proof of address; a government photo ID for each witness; the wedding invitation card or a certificate from the person who performed the ceremony; and two wedding photographs. The registration fee is ₹200 if the application is made within 90 days of the marriage and ₹1,000 after 90 days. Appointments are booked on the portal, and walk-in applications are taken only on Thursdays. The certificate is issued on the same day if all documents are in order. Additional certified copies cost ₹100 each. If either spouse was previously married, a divorce decree or the death certificate of the former spouse must also be produced. Registration is not refused because of a delay, but marriages more than five years old need an affidavit from both spouses.

title: Grievance redressal and service timelines
text: Civic complaints can be registered on the 24-hour helpline 1800 270 4410, on the citizen portal or at any ward office, and every complaint gets a docket number by SMS. The service standards are as follows. Garbage not collected is cleared the same day. A dead animal is removed within 24 hours. A streetlight that is not working is repaired within 72 hours. A water pipeline leak or a blocked drain is attended to within 48 hours. A pothole is filled within 10 working days, except from June to September, when only temporary patching is done. A request for mosquito fogging is handled within 3 working days. If a complaint is not resolved within its service standard, it is escalated automatically to the assistant commissioner of the ward, and after 7 more days to the zonal deputy commissioner. A complaint marked as closed can be reopened by the citizen within 7 days if the work was not actually done. The zonal deputy commissioner holds an open public hearing every Monday from 11 am to 1 pm at each zone office, and no appointment is needed.

title: Ward offices, zone offices and counter hours
text: The city has 64 wards grouped into four zones. Ward offices are open from 10 am to 5:30 pm, Monday to Friday, and from 10 am to 1:30 pm on Saturdays, and they are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Cash counters at ward offices close at 4 pm on weekdays and at 1 pm on Saturdays. Ward offices handle property tax payments, birth and death registration, pet registration and complaints. The four zone offices are open from 10 am to 6 pm, Monday to Saturday, and are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays; they handle building plans, trade licences, marriage registration and tax objections, and their cash counters stay open until 5 pm. In July and January, when property tax instalments fall due, ward office cash counters stay open until 7 pm on the last five working days of the month and open from 10 am to 2 pm on the last Sunday of the month. Payments on the citizen portal can be made at any time, and a payment made online before midnight on a due date is treated as on time. Cash payments above ₹20,000 are not accepted at any counter.

title: Tree felling and road-cutting permission
text: Permission is needed to cut down any tree with a trunk girth of more than 30 cm at 1.3 metres above the ground, whether the tree stands on public land or inside a private compound. The application fee is ₹200 per tree, and a refundable deposit of ₹5,000 per tree is collected. The deposit is refunded once the applicant has planted three saplings for every tree felled and the saplings have survived for one year. The tree officer inspects the site and decides within 21 days; a tree that is dead or in danger of falling is dealt with within 72 hours. Pruning does not need permission unless more than one third of the canopy is removed. Cutting a tree without permission carries a fine of ₹25,000 per tree. Permission to cut a public road, for example to lay a private pipe or cable, is given by the zonal engineer within 10 working days, and the road restoration charge is paid in advance at ₹1,100 per running metre for tar roads and ₹1,600 per running metre for concrete roads. No road-cutting is allowed from 1 June to 30 September except for emergency repairs.
